## Part 1 — How-to pages

### P01 — Join a group

Open the group's page from its link or your invitation. Check that it is the group you meant to join.

If **Join** is offered, choose it and complete the joining confirmation if shown.

If you see **Request to join**, open it, follow the instructions about a message and choose **Send request**. This asks an organizer for approval; sending a request does not make you a member.

If you have an invitation, choose **Accept** on that invitation and complete any joining steps shown. If none of these options is available, ask the group's organizers how to join.

### P02 — Write a post

Open your group's **Stream**. Find **Say something to the group** and write your post there. Check the group and the audience shown before you choose **Post**.

A post is for sharing something with its chosen audience. Avoid putting information there that those people should not see. If you need to add a lasting reference document, use the library instead.

If the post box is missing or you cannot submit, ask an organizer about your access. You do not have to post to use the site.

### P03 — Add a page or file to the library

To write a page, choose **New Topic** in the create menu, if available. Write your page, complete the required fields and check its group and audience. Choose **Create topic**.

To upload a file, open your group's **Import** tab, choose **Upload files**, then **Choose files**. Check **Who can see these pages?** and complete the required fields. Tick the rights box only if you have permission to share the files. Choose **Import 1 file**, or the button showing your file count.

Use selectable text for assistant answers; it cannot read an image-only scan. A changed file becomes a new document; it does not replace the old one. If these controls are missing, ask an organizer.

### P04 — Ask the assistant and check sources

On your group's page, open the assistant at the bottom right. It is not shown on the **Import** tab. Ask a question about the library.

When an answer includes **Sources**, open a numbered source link and check the original passage. Does it support the answer? An answer can be wrong. If no useful source appears, read the documents or ask an organizer.

Your question and passages used to answer it are sent to the AI service. Preparing pages for search also sends their text to that service, even if you never open the assistant.

The assistant advises. It does not carry out decisions or payments for you.

### P05 — Find an event and respond

Open your group's **Events**. Choose an event and read its time, place and instructions. **Calendar** gives you a calendar view; **List** takes you back.

If **Enroll** is available and you want to attend, choose it. If the event offers **Request to enroll**, follow that request instead; a request needs approval. Follow any further instructions shown.

**Enrolled** shows an existing sign-up. If your plans change and **Cancel enrollment** is available, use it.

Some events have different sign-up arrangements. Follow the event's instructions or ask its organizer if no sign-up action is offered.

### P06 — Answer a quick poll

Open **Quick polls** in your group. Choose a question, read the choices, select your answer and choose **Answer**.

Once you choose **Answer**, your answer stays: a quick poll does not let you take it back or change it, so check your choice first. If offered, **See answers so far** shows the current responses.

A quick poll checks how members lean. It does not settle a decision for the group. If the question is closed or the answer controls are unavailable, ask the organizer rather than treating it as an unanswered form.

### P07 — Change which emails you get

Open your account menu and choose **Settings**. Find **Email notifications**. For each kind of notification shown, choose the frequency you want, then choose **Save**.

Choose **Never** for a kind you do not want by email. These choices concern the notifications listed on that form; they do not promise to stop every email about your account or the site.

If the settings are missing or an email keeps arriving unexpectedly, ask an organizer for help. Describe the kind of email, without forwarding private material unnecessarily.

### P08 — Leave a group

Open the group's page. Open **Joined**, choose **Leave group**, then confirm with **Leave this house**.

Check the group name before confirming. Leaving a group is different from closing your site account. It does not erase the group's records or messages you have already contributed.

For questions about your own pages, access after leaving or removing records, ask the organizers. If you cannot find the leaving controls, ask them for help.

### P09 — Report a problem

For a problem with an imported library page, open that page and choose **Report a problem with this page**.

Choose a reason under **What's the problem?** Use **Details (optional)** to explain what is wrong and where it appears. Add **Your email (optional)** if you would like a reply. Then choose **Send report**.

Your report goes to the site's organizers and the host. They can see the email address you include. Share only what they need to understand the problem.

This link is on imported pages. For other content, ask your group's organizers. For a site or sign-in problem, use **Get help**.

### P10 — Get help

Choose **Get help** in the footer. Ask your group's organizers first about group settings, documents or access.

For a site or sign-in problem, use the email contact shown on that help page. Say what you were trying to do and what happened. Do not send sign-in codes or passwords.

If someone else got into your account, open **Hacked or phished?** for the account-safety instructions.

### P11 — Respond to a decision

If your group has voting on and your voting access is already set up, open **Votes** and choose the proposal you want to read. Read its text, deadline and voting rules before responding.

When the form is available, choose **For**, **Against** or **Abstain** under **How do you vote?** Choose **Cast your vote**, follow the confirmation shown and check that your response is recorded.

If **Change your vote** is offered while voting is open, use it to choose again and complete the confirmation.

If the form is unavailable, read the explanation and ask an organizer. This page describes the voting screen; your group still needs to agree how it makes decisions.

### P12 — See what the fund holds

If the fund is on for your group, open **Fund**. Read the **Balances** and the update time beside them.

Choose **Refresh balances** to request another reading. If the page shows older balances or says it could not read them, do not treat the display as a current balance. An unreadable amount is not proof that the fund is empty.

If the fund is not ready or no balance is available, read the explanation and ask an organizer. Reading this page does not make a payment.

## Part 2 — First-visit tour words

Six stops per version. Titles have at most five words; bodies at most 25. These are **new build words**, not a claim that a tour exists. Use the six targets below for both versions. None of the selectors supplied here is guessed; targets without selectors are named source elements for the builder to resolve.

### House version

| Stop | Title | Body | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Your house stream | Open Stream to read what your house is sharing. Use the post box when you have something to add. | T1 |
| 2 | What's coming up | Open Events for your house's events. Read an event's time, place and sign-up instructions before responding. | T2 |
| 3 | Read the library | Open Topics for your house's library pages and files. You can read them without opening the assistant. | T3 |
| 4 | Ask and check | Ask about your house's documents. The assistant can be wrong. Open a numbered link under Sources and check the original passage. | T4 |
| 5 | Your other groups | Open Groups on your profile to return to your groups. A new group may need organizer approval or an invitation. | T5 |
| 6 | Help with this site | Need a hand? Open Get help or ask the assistant “how do I” questions about using this site. | T6 |

## Part 3 — Checks for the assistant

These are acceptance procedures, **not executed results**. Index only the appropriate member pages. Ask as an ordinary member who can read them; open each returned citation and confirm the cited passage supports the answer. A correct-sounding answer without the required readable page is a failure. Do not index this expected-answer table.

| Question | Required cited page | What the answer must preserve |
|---|---|---|
| How do I join a group that needs approval? | P01 — Join a group | Request to join → follow message instructions → Send request; sending is not approval. No automatic membership promise. |
| How do I write a post in my group? | P02 — Write a post | Stream → Say something to the group → check audience → Post. No invented Send button. |
| How do I add a file the assistant can read? | P03 — Add a page or file to the library | Import → Upload files → Choose files; permission/rights and audience checks; use selectable text; the full file-count import button. No immediate-indexing promise. |
| How do I check whether the assistant's answer is right? | P04 — Ask the assistant and check sources | Open a numbered link under Sources and read the original passage; an answer can be wrong. No claimed action or certainty. |
| How do I stop one kind of notification email? | P07 — Change which emails you get | Account Settings → Email notifications → Never for that category → Save. No promise to stop all mail. |
| How do I leave a group? | P08 — Leave a group | Joined → Leave group → Leave this house. No erasure, account-closure or blanket later-access promise. |

Run these two questions with **only the supplied how-to pages in scope**, or a controlled library containing no answer to them. They test the coverage boundary, not denial of information that another real page actually contains.

| Uncovered question | Required response | Citation rule |
|---|---|---|
| Who has the spare key to our meeting room? | “I couldn't find that in the library pages I can use. Ask your group's organizers.” | No invented person or source; no citation to a how-to page as evidence of who has a key. |
| What did our group agree about quiet hours last month? | “I couldn't find that agreement in the library pages I can use. Ask your group's organizers or check the meeting notes.” | No invented rule or decision; no citation that merely explains how to use the site. |

Finally confirm that disabled-feature pages and builder notes cannot appear as member guidance or search answers. P11's access/setup and pending house-screen rewrite, P12's stale/unreadable states, T5's final anchor and the absent replay remain explicit handoff conditions. Nothing here records a live pass.
